headline: Every bottle checked, at 850 a minute.
label: #F3EFE4
heroLede: Bundaberg Brewed Drinks is family owned, and its $120 million Master Brewery on Kay McDuff Drive can fill around 850 bottles a minute of brews like Ginger Beer. At that speed a crooked cap or a wrong label is gone before anyone sees it. This is what a camera check could look like on your bottling line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every cap is on, straight and fully closed. A loose cap lets a brewed drink go flat and shows up as a complaint long after the bottle has left Bundaberg.
labelLede: Ginger Beer and Diet Ginger Beer bottles look almost the same until you read the label, and the wrong one is a sugar claim that is not true. The camera checks every bottle carries the right label for the run, straight and intact.
codeLede: The best-before and batch code has to be right and readable on every bottle. The system reads the printed code and compares it with the brew and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Glass fragments, caps and carton offcuts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four crooked caps in fifteen minutes on Line 1. Check the capper.
